ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA, each met. (1) An approval binds draft id, draft digest, project id, repository, branch and base commit, and is rechecked against the repository as it is at approval time — the digest is RECOMPUTED, never read from the stored draft. (2) A changed draft, a moved repository state, a different project and a different repository each invalidate it and fail closed, all proven by test. (3) The implementer cannot approve; submitting an objective cannot; generating a draft cannot; a filename cannot; prose saying 'approved' cannot. (4) Approval produced a NEW post-V3 plan record and left projectos-v3.plan.json byte-identical — verified against the closed baseline d30dca0. (5) PLAN READY is recomputed independently by the existing evaluator; the record's own status string is never trusted.

THE PLAN DIGEST covers plan material only — vision, definition of complete, success standard, scope, environments, phases, conflicts, owner decisions and planning sources. Editing an unrelated file does NOT invalidate an approval; changing one word of the plan DOES. Both directions are proven, and the digest held identical across five commits and across repeat runs.

A HOLE IN THE READINESS EVALUATOR, found while wiring this up and fixed here: evaluatePlanReady checked that approvalAuthority said 'owner' and that approvedBy was not the implementer, and ANY other name satisfied both — so a plan approved by a stranger read as an owner-authority approval. The approver must now BE the recorded owner, or the plan must carry an approvalDelegation from that owner to exactly that person, scoped to this project, carrying plan approval only and no protected action. Eight escalation attempts are proven to fail.

CLOSURE AUTHORITY IS RECORDED SEPARATELY FROM PLAN APPROVAL, on purpose: approving a plan and closing a phase are different authorities, and one record granting both would be a way to widen either by editing the other. The validator refuses them sharing a scope.

MUTATIONS, 25/25 killed: 11 on the approval mechanism, 6 on the authority boundary in the governance engine, 7 on the self-review fixes, 1 on the phase-ordering fix. One documented survivor — a current-state schema guard that no input can reach while the plan schema passes — kept and annotated in code as unreachable rather than deleted to flatter a score.

REVIEWS — STATED PRECISELY, NOT OVERCLAIMED. An implementer self-review of the new code, performed before the mechanism was ever used, found four real defects and all were fixed and mutation-proven: a committed-ness check that then read the WORKING TREE, so an innocuous record could be committed while a different one was believed; command-line ids joined straight onto a path, so a path-shaped decision id read outside the project and would have written the consumption marker there; an approval able to write over any existing file; and an activation that would have dropped the outgoing completion evidence and resurrected the closed programme's phases at the next objective. The delegated gatekeeper reviewed the substance at the plan-authority gate and issued the approval decision. NO independent ECC review agent ran in this session. 0 unresolved CRITICAL, 0 unresolved HIGH.

CARRY-FORWARD: tamperProof is false and stays false — anything that can write a file can write these records, and the boundary is that they must exist as distinct reviewable artefacts and must be COMMITTED, so a forgery is a visible diff at the owner's gate; planVersion is fixed at 1.0 and supersession for a second approval at the same path is not implemented, with the command refusing to overwrite an existing plan record, which fails closed; .projectops/drafts/ is gitignored, so the approved draft is regenerable rather than committed, and a reviewer wanting the exact bytes must regenerate them.
headedProofPass is false and the plan does not require a browser proof for this phase (requiredBrowserProof false). No owner-facing surface was changed by this phase.

PROTECTED EFFECTS: NONE. The one authority-bearing act — activating the plan — was performed by the runtime on the strength of a committed decision by the delegated authority, and is recorded with its consumedAt marker. No production, database, external send, payment, credential, installation, service, ACL, registry or ProgramData action. No force push, no history rewrite, no merge to a protected branch.
